claims: C1 autonomy must be bounded by a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user
C2 the scope defines which sub-goals the assistant may pursue
C3 the scope defines acceptable side effects and, if applicable, how to handle tradeoffs between them
C4 the scope defines when the assistant must pause for clarification or approval

concepts.name: scope_of_autonomy
concepts.gloss: the agreed-upon boundary of the assistant's autonomy, defining which sub-goals it may pursue, acceptable side effects, and when it must pause for clarification or approval

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: the assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text refers to 'the assistant' without defining it

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries the root level of instruction authority, the highest in the hierarchy; it cannot be overridden by system, developer or user instructions
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text does not itself state the authority level

concepts.name: shared_scope
concepts.gloss: the scope of autonomy is clear and mutually understood by both the assistant and the user

concepts.name: subgoal_in_scope
concepts.gloss: the sub-goal is one the scope of autonomy permits the assistant to pursue

concepts.name: side_effect_acceptable
concepts.gloss: the side effect is one the scope of autonomy marks as acceptable

concepts.name: tradeoff_handling_specified
concepts.gloss: the scope of autonomy specifies how to handle this tradeoff between acceptable side effects

concepts.name: requires_pause
concepts.gloss: the situation is one in which the scope of autonomy requires the assistant to pause for clarification or approval

ontology.gloss: S is a scope of autonomy that is clear and mutually understood between the assistant and the user

asserts.read_back: pursuing sub-goal % is permitted when % is a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user and % is within that scope
causing side effect % is permitted when % is a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user and % is an acceptable side effect under that scope
handling tradeoff % is permitted when % is a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user and % is a tradeoff whose handling is specified by that scope

pausing for clarification or approval is obliged when % is a clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user and % is a situation that scope requires a pause for

closure.reason: the clause says the scope defines which sub-goals the assistant may pursue, so a sub-goal outside the scope is not permitted
the clause says the scope defines acceptable side effects, so a side effect not marked acceptable is not permitted
the clause says the scope defines how to handle tradeoffs, so a tradeoff not covered by the scope is not permitted to be handled autonomously
the clause obliges a pause only when the scope requires it; it does not forbid pausing in other situations
